question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 16 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 26 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 16 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of times = LCM(16, 26, 16) = 208 units.

Combined efficiency = (208 ÷ 16) + (208 ÷ 26) + (208 ÷ 16) = 13 + 8 + 13 = 34 units/hour.

Time taken together = Total work ÷ Combined efficiency = 208 ÷ 34 = 104/17 = 6 2/17 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 2/17 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A = 16 hours

Time taken by Pipe B = 26 hours

Time taken by Pipe C = 16 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Efficiency of Pipe A, B, and C together = 13 + 8 + 13 = 34 units/hour

⇒ Time taken by all three pipes together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 208 ÷ 34

⇒ Time taken = 104 ÷ 17 = 6 2/17 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 6 2/17 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inlet vs Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills a tank and its work/efficiency is treated as positive. An outlet pipe empties a tank and its work/efficiency is treated as negative.

Combined Work of Pipes

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours and another fills it in y hours, their combined time to fill the tank together is (x × y) ÷ (x + y) hours.

Part of Tank Filled

If a pipe requires n hours to completely fill an empty tank, the part of the tank filled by the pipe in 1 hour is 1/n.
